The first native Rust release of [nesterm](https://github.com/kathoc/nesterm):
play NES games in a terminal using the 95 printable ASCII characters.
The downloaded executable requires no Rust, Cargo, or Node.js installation.

## Downloads

| System | Archive |
|---|---|
| Linux x86-64 (static musl) | [nesterm-v0.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz](https://github.com/vertigo-red/nesterm-rust/releases/download/v0.1.0/nesterm-v0.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz) |
| macOS Apple Silicon | [nesterm-v0.1.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz](https://github.com/vertigo-red/nesterm-rust/releases/download/v0.1.0/nesterm-v0.1.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz) |
| macOS Intel | [nesterm-v0.1.0-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz](https://github.com/vertigo-red/nesterm-rust/releases/download/v0.1.0/nesterm-v0.1.0-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz) |
| Windows x86-64 | [nesterm-v0.1.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip](https://github.com/vertigo-red/nesterm-rust/releases/download/v0.1.0/nesterm-v0.1.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) |

Extract the archive, open a terminal in its directory, and run:

```sh
./nesterm /path/to/game.nes --size 64x30 --fps 60
```

On Windows, use Windows Terminal and `./nesterm.exe C:/path/to/game.nes`.
Bring your own `.nes` ROM; no games are included.
Linux is statically linked and has no glibc dependency. Windows includes the
static C runtime. macOS binaries target macOS 13 or newer and are tested on
macOS 15. They are not Apple-signed or notarized; Gatekeeper may require approval
in System Settings → Privacy & Security before their first launch.

[SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/vertigo-red/nesterm-rust/releases/download/v0.1.0/SHA256SUMS)
contains SHA-256 checksums for all four archives. Download it alongside your
archive and compare the matching line with `sha256sum ARCHIVE` on Linux,
`shasum -a 256 ARCHIVE` on macOS, or `Get-FileHash ARCHIVE -Algorithm SHA256`
in PowerShell.

## Features

- 40×25 and 64×30 grids; shape and brightness-ramp rendering; color or monochrome.
- Native Rust NES emulation with tetanes-core 0.17.0.
- Arrows/WASD, X/Z, Enter, Space; P to pause; Q or Ctrl-C to quit.
- Kitty keyboard protocol on Unix and a timed fallback for legacy terminals.
- ANSI frame differences, asciicast v2 recording, terminal cleanup on exit.

## Validation and limits

The release workflow tests all four native targets and runs seven real PTY
integration scenarios on Linux and both macOS architectures. Renderer tests
compare 72 complete reference frames with the upstream JavaScript renderer.
Tests use a generated original NROM; commercial games have not been validated.

Audio and save-file persistence are not implemented. Trainer-ROMs and NES 2.0
exponent-encoded PRG/CHR sizes are unsupported. Mapper support and gameplay may
differ from the JavaScript core. Windows is build- and test-verified; interactive
PTY tests cover Linux and macOS.

Each archive includes the application license, glyph notices, dependency
licenses, Rust standard-library notices, and the unmodified source of the
MPL-2.0 dependency `option-ext`.
